preview: Yash Shroff shares his internship interview experience at Fractal, detailing the online aptitude test, a technical interview with problem-solving and project discussions, and the final HR round.
content: Location: Mumbai Stipend: 30k Interview Experience Yash Shroff Fractal Conducted 3 rounds : Followed by HR round. First one Being the online test round. Second was the interview round. Online Round: The first round was composed of 4 sections: Time was a major constraint here, 70 questions were to be solved in 75 minutes. 4 sections : Data Analysis Logical Reasoning Quantitative Reasoning English Where Data Analysis being the toughest and English being the easiest .As there was a lot of time constraint, I saw my time ticking away and decided to solve the English section first as it had only 10 questions and seemed easy to me. Followed by quantative reasoning and Logical reasoning , both the sections demanded good aptitude skills , I started solving whichever I felt took the least time , around 4 - 5 questions I had left for review. I rushed to them as soon as I realized there was little to no time left , but I ended up missing them. It was a big mistake as I should atleast not left them unanswered. Finally results came out and out of 200 students 23 were selected for the interview round. You now Know I was one of them as Ill tell you about the Interview Round now. The Data Analysis was the tricky part, It demanded patience and calmness as the questions took time to analyze , understand and then solve . Some of them were tough and most of them had moderate difficulty. Included various Pie charts , Graphs , Tabular data ,etc. And Questions were asked on the basis of these data models. Since it took time I had forgotten that I had 4 questions remaining to be answered in the Logical sections. Interview Round: The round started with I giving her a brief Introduction about myself. She seemed like she had a lot to ask about my CV but ended up asking a different question. The first question was- Lets suppose a user has to Login into a page , So for that he/she will be entering a password. How will you check if the password entered by the user is correct or incorrect? I hadnt come across a question like this so I started thinking out loud. Told her about my approaches that the password input would be a string , I will be basically comparing the password’s string with user’s input , but that was not all. We had quite a long discussion on this ,it included data structures used , maps etc. Even Though I felt my answer was not 100% correct , she seemed to like the way I was approaching her counter questions , without getting stuck and figuring out them one by one. The second question was regarding my project , where I gave her a gist of Socket-IO. She had some counter questions here too and I answered each of them thoroughly. Followed by a SQL query which I was not confident at the beginning that I would be be able to solve but I did not show her this, instead I started explaining to her how I would solve , I took my time and I successfully solved the Query.(Question used concept of inner join, aggregate functions and other clauses like ‘ GROUP BY’,etc) She then asked me a puzzle which was not that tricky , I solved that puzzle piece by piece and reached the optimal answer. I told her that I can optimize this even more and asked her for some more time . So she smiled at me and told me that it cannot be done. After that she asked me if she selects me in her team and had to decide on which team would she allocate me and gave some options.To that I replied about how I believe "learning" is valuable and it should never stop, I told her I look forward to learning new technologies , finally concluded that hence I am flexible to all the requirements at hand. I had written ‘Blockchain’ on my CV so she asked me to explain her everything about Blockchain but in such a way that a person not knowing a thing about Blockchain would understand. I was happy to talk about this and she saw it on my face. I explained her everything from scratch and she seemed satisfied , I explained her everything like I would have explained to my friend.The discussion went long and we were 15 minutes above the deadline. So other candidates after their first round, if selected were told to wait for to know if they were selected for the HR round , but since my round went overtime , she told me that , Yash Check your mail, you will now have your HR round in few minutes. Not being in suspense about the selection felt nice. HR Round: This Round also started with me giving a brief intro about myself to the HR He asked me questions related to my projects, then I ended up sharing my screen and gave him a tour of the project. He was completely satisfied and was happy with the explanation. He asked me if I am a person who prefers to work in a team or individually (he told me he personally is more productive individually) but I gave my reasons and explained how i would rather work with a team. Further he asked me on how would my best friend describe me? Asked me about my weakness, Do I get angry easily? Then he went on to ask me about the courses I have done other than academics, I told him about DSA and also about trading (technical analysis) I told him about how charts fascinate me. I ended up asking him a question about how projects are in Fractal and emerging importance of data. He explained me in brief and that was all, as far as I remember this round ended quite smoothly. Preparation and Tips: You can read other interviews for tips and prep source as everyone has written them to the point. DSA>> Confidence>> English>> Three suggestions from my side: Fod ke aao , bhot chances deta hai VJTI
